correctness.rationale: Fixed rank-one column and row fibers have Hilbertian finite-support images. Strict singularity therefore makes each such restriction compact. Two finite-dimensional Calkin-quotient reductions then force compact left and right coefficients, while compact coefficients give a norm limit of finite-rank superoperators. The contrapositive produces an infinite-dimensional complemented rank-one fiber on which every noncompact elementary operator is bounded below.

originality.rationale: Targeted exact and synonymous searches located classical work on elementary mappings into ideals, structural and compact elementary-operator results, and strict singularity of single two-sided multiplications on full operator algebras, but no matching theorem giving ordinary strict-singularity/FSS/compactness collapse for finite elementary sums on Banach norm ideals together with a complemented rank-one witness. The most relevant 1984 ideal paper and older compactness literature remain a documented residual risk.

value.rationale: The result gives a class-level structural obstruction: finite elementary superoperators cannot realize noncompact strictly singular behavior on any normalized Banach norm ideal, and every failure of compactness is already visible on a 1-complemented Hilbertian rank-one slice, yielding uniform Bernstein-number lower bounds.
